analysis.investment_thesis: Capillary is a marginally profitable SaaS business priced for perfection at 420x earnings, yet delivers only 2.56% ROE and negative free cash flow of ₹94 Cr in FY2025 despite a reported ₹13 Cr net profit — a dangerous divergence. A wonderful business it is not; paying 420x for it is simply irrational.
key_strengths: Strong revenue CAGR of 36.7% (₹171 Cr → ₹598 Cr) shows genuine market demand for loyalty SaaS
Low Debt/Equity of 0.17 with ₹201 Cr cash provides balance sheet breathing room
Finally turned EBITDA positive (₹72 Cr) and net profitable (₹13 Cr) in FY2025 after years of losses
key_risks: Valuation is absurd: P/E 420x and EV/EBITDA 52x for a business earning ₹13 Cr net profit on ₹4,492 Cr market cap
FCF deeply negative at -₹94 Cr in FY2025 despite reported profit — cash earnings don't exist yet
ROE of 2.56% and ROCE of 2.88% are far below my minimum threshold of 15%; this destroys shareholder value per rupee deployed
red_flags: Net profit of ₹13 Cr vs. negative FCF of ₹94 Cr in the same year — aggressive accruals or working capital deterioration
Company was loss-making 4 of the last 5 years; single-year profitability is unproven and razor-thin
Operating margin of only 5.2% for a SaaS company signals weak pricing power and competitive commoditization
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Capillary Technologies competes in the loyalty and customer engagement SaaS space against Salesforce, Adobe, and Oracle — giants with far superior resources, distribution, and moats. Its 5.2% operating margin tells me this is not a business with meaningful pricing power. I need at least 15% ROE consistently to get excited; Capillary delivers 2.56%. The company burned cash for four straight years (cumulative net losses of ~₹269 Cr from FY2021–2024) and has only just eked out ₹13 Cr net profit in FY2025 — yet the market has priced this as if decades of compounding prosperity are guaranteed at 420x earnings.

The cash flow statement is disqualifying. A business that reports ₹13 Cr profit but burns ₹94 Cr in FCF and ₹46 Cr in operating cash flow is not a business I can trust. My favorite holding period is forever, but only for businesses where earnings are real and cash is king. Capillary's capital intensity is rising (capex grew from ₹28 Cr to ₹47 Cr in three years) while returns on capital remain microscopic. At ₹566 per share and ₹4,492 Cr market cap, you are paying 7.5x revenue for a company with no demonstrated ability to generate durable free cash flow. I would not buy this at any price close to current levels.
